newsitem.title: USA: Salomon sees U.S. stocks clipped by China debate.
newsitem.headline: Salomon sees U.S. stocks clipped by China debate.

text.p: The debate in the U.S. Congress over the renewal of China's Most Favored Nation trade status could add to pressure on U.S. stocks, dragging the S&P 500 index to the 700 level, a Salomon Brothers analyst said.
The index was up about six points at 764 on Monday.

The threat of a trade spat between the U.S. and China would undermine one of the principal underlying theses of the bull market: a high growth world with a surplus of labor, Salomon chief equity strategist David Shulman said in a report.
"Should fears of a 'trade shock' become widespread, then the S&P 500 could soon find itself testing the 700 level," a summary of the report issued by Salomon said.
Shulman noted that the stock market is already under pressure from Federal Reserve interest rate tightening and rising interest rates in the bond market.
Shulman believes the MFN will ultimately be approved after a high-profile debate, the report said.
The analyst said he was retaining "China-dependent" Boeing Co on Salomon's recommended list "with great trepidation."

He said he is recommending domestic companies over international ones in the near term, naming Mead Corp, Reynolds Metals Co, W.W. Grainger Inc, Hilton Hotels Corp, Marriott International Inc, Home Depot Inc, Costco Cos Inc and Cox Communications Inc.
Shulman also listed international petroleum companies Dresser Industries Inc and British Petroleum Plc among recommended stocks.
